questions.question: How many squares does the apples bar have?
questions.explain: Count the filled squares from the bottom of the bar to the top. There are 5, so 5 kids chose apples. The trap is counting the grid lines instead of the squares, which gives 6.

questions.question: The graph shows pets seen in the schoolyard. How many squares does the dogs bar have?
questions.explain: Each square stands for one pet, so 8 squares means 8 dogs. If you count the grid lines instead of the filled squares, you get 9, which is the common slip.

questions.question: How many squares does the crackers bar have?
questions.explain: Look at the crackers bar and count its squares: there are 4. Each square is one vote, so 4 kids chose crackers. Counting lines instead of squares gives 5.

questions.question: The graph shows favourite colours. How many squares does the blue bar have?
questions.explain: One square equals one vote, so 10 squares means 10 kids picked blue. A quick way to trip up is counting the grid lines, which gives 11.

questions.question: Maya's class voted on where to go this weekend. How many squares does the park bar have?
questions.explain: Each square is one vote, so the park bar with 7 squares means 7 kids picked the park. Don't count the grid lines — that would give 8.

questions.question: The garden club planted flowers and made a bar graph. How many squares does the tulips bar have?
questions.explain: One square means one flower, so 6 squares is 6 tulips. A common slip is counting the grid lines, which would give 7 instead of 6.

questions.question: Sam made a bar graph of the shoes in the classroom closet. How many squares does the sneakers bar have?
questions.explain: Count the squares in the sneakers bar: there are 12, so 12 sneakers are in the closet. Counting the grid lines instead of the squares gives 13.

questions.question: The library made a bar graph of books borrowed last week. How many squares does the picture books bar have?
questions.explain: One square is one book, so 9 squares means 9 picture books were borrowed. The trap is counting grid lines instead of squares, which gives 10.

questions.question: Leo reads the soccer bar and says, 'Seven kids play soccer.' What did Leo do wrong?
options: He counted grid lines, not squares.
He read the baseball bar instead.
He counted each square as two kids.
He added one square to the bar.
questions.explain: The soccer bar has 6 squares, so 6 kids play soccer. Leo counted the grid lines (which is 7) instead of the filled squares.

questions.question: The vet's office made a bar graph of pets. A new cat comes in, making the cat bar one square taller. How many squares will the cat bar have?
questions.explain: The cat bar starts at 7 squares. One more cat adds 1 square, so 7 + 1 = 8. Counting grid lines instead of squares would give 9.

questions.question: A bar graph shows shells collected at the beach. One more shell is added to Jade's pile. How many squares will Jade's bar have?
questions.explain: Jade's bar starts at 4 squares. One more shell adds 1 square, so 4 + 1 = 5. Counting the grid lines instead of the squares would give 6.

questions.question: A bar graph shows books in each box. The math box will have 3 more squares than the science box. How many squares will the math bar have?
questions.explain: The science box has 7 squares. Three more means 7 + 3 = 10. Reading the wrong bar (like art at 11) is a common slip.
